rawAnswer: {"story":{"what":"The change hardens TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo so that invalid key setups no longer throw. After reporting a mixed int/string key diagnostic, it now skips that member (continue). It also adds a member to intMembers or stringMembers only if the key is not already there, so duplicate keys no longer call Dictionary.Add twice. It also tightens the condition for flushing deferred non-public-member diagnostics from || to &&. In the code, the analyzer path for these types could throw on duplicate or mixed keys: Dictionary.Add with a duplicate key, or intKey!.Value on a null value. That would abort analysis instead of reporting diagnostics.
